# OpenFullPage — full reference for machine readers

> A free, open-source Chrome extension that captures a whole web page of any
> length as one image, opens it in a real editor to annotate and redact, and
> saves or copies it. It makes no network requests at all.

Canonical site: https://palworks.github.io/openfullpage-site/
Extension source: https://github.com/PalWorks/OpenFullPage---Screenshot-Annotate-Save
Website source: https://github.com/PalWorks/openfullpage-site
Publisher: PalWorks — https://palworks.ai
Licence: GPL-3.0-only
Platform: Google Chrome 116 or newer, Manifest V3
Operating systems: Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS
Price: free, permanently. No paid tier, no trial, no account, no advertising.
Last reviewed: 2026-09-11

The repository README is the authoritative and more frequently updated feature
list. This file summarises it and the website; where they differ, the README is
correct.

## Entity definition

OpenFullPage is a browser extension in the screenshot and screen-capture
category. Its distinguishing property is that it has no network access
whatsoever, enforced by the browser rather than promised in a policy, and that
every privacy property is checked automatically on every commit.

It is not a service, has no server component, no account system and no cloud
storage. Nothing it captures is transmitted anywhere.

## Capabilities

### Capture
- A whole page of any length as a single stitched image.
- Visible area only.
- A single selected element.
- Sticky and fixed headers appear once, at the top, instead of repeating down
  every screenful.
- Lazy-loaded content below the fold is loaded and given time to settle before
  its screenful is taken.
- Retina displays and browser zoom are handled by deriving the scale from the
  captured bitmap rather than assuming it.
- Same-origin iframes are expanded to full height before capture.
- Scrollbars are cropped out rather than stitched in.
- The page is restored afterwards, including scroll position and sticky
  headers, even if the capture fails partway.
- Capture steps have deadlines, so a page that never finishes loading cannot
  hang the extension.

### Edit
- The capture opens in a real editor. Shapes remain live objects: select, drag,
  resize by handles, restyle and delete.
- Annotation shapes include arrows, lines, boxes, ellipses, highlighter and
  more, plus text and numbered steps.
- Text is multi-line with family, size, weight, style and alignment controls.
- Stroke weight, dash style, arrowheads and corner style are adjustable.
- Border and fill colours are separate controls, with opacity on fill.
- Crop proposes a region with handles, confirmed or abandoned explicitly.
- Multiple selection, undo and redo covering moves and resizes as well as
  drawing.
- Keyboard shortcuts throughout, including arrow-key nudging.
- Theme follows the system, or can be set to light or dark.

### Redaction
Redaction resamples the pixels underneath rather than drawing a blur over them,
and the export is flattened, so a saved image has no original hiding beneath
the redaction. Magnification operates on a redacted copy, never the original.

### Output
- Saves to image and document formats including PNG and JPEG.
- Copies to the clipboard.
- Filenames are built from the page URL and the date, and are editable before
  saving.

## The five enforced rules

Each of these is checked on every commit and fails the build if broken.

1. **No network access.** The manifest declares `connect-src 'none'`. Chrome
   blocks fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and beacons at the browser level, so
   the extension cannot transmit anything even if its code tried to.
2. **No remote code.** No `eval`, no `new Function`, no update server, no
   remotely fetched configuration.
3. **No dependencies and no build step.** The installed package is byte-identical
   to the public source, and the build proves it by diffing the two.
4. **Minimal permissions at install.** Only `activeTab`, `scripting` and
   `storage`.
5. **No synced storage.** `chrome.storage.sync` is never used, so settings never
   leave the machine that made them.

## Permissions in detail

| Permission | When | What it allows | What it does not allow |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activeTab` | At install | Read the current page, and only after the toolbar button is clicked on it | Any access to other tabs, or to this tab before you click |
| `scripting` | At install | Run the scrolling and measuring code, only where `activeTab` already allows it | Running anywhere you have not invoked the extension |
| `storage` | At install | Remember settings locally | Syncing anything; `chrome.storage.sync` is never used |
| `downloads` | First save | Write the image to your downloads folder | Reading your downloads, or writing anywhere else |
| `webNavigation` plus site access | Optional, off by default | Capture the full contents of cross-origin iframes | Sending anything anywhere; the CSP still blocks all outbound requests |

Even with every permission granted, the content security policy still blocks
every outbound request. The permissions allow reading a page. None of them
allows sending what was read anywhere.

## How to verify the claims yourself

1. Capture a full page with DevTools open on the Network tab. It stays empty.
2. Read the manifest. `connect-src 'none'` is declared there.
3. Run the checks the build runs. They are in the repository.
4. Diff the packaged extension against the public source. They match.

Full instructions: https://palworks.github.io/openfullpage-site/enforced.html

## Frequently asked questions

**Is OpenFullPage free?**
Yes, permanently. There is no paid tier, no trial and no account. It is open
source under GPL-3.0.

**Where do my screenshots go?**
To your downloads folder, or your clipboard. Nowhere else is possible, because
the extension has no network access.

**Does OpenFullPage upload my screenshots anywhere?**
No, and it cannot. The manifest sets `connect-src 'none'`, so Chrome itself
refuses to carry any outbound request the extension might attempt.

**Does it work on very long pages?**
Yes. That is its primary purpose. It scrolls the page, captures each screenful
and stitches them into one image, however far the page runs.

**What about sticky headers that repeat?**
They are held still during capture, so they appear once at the top rather than
repeating down the image. This is the failure mode that makes naive full-page
capture unusable on many sites.

**How do I redact private information?**
Use the redaction tool before saving. It resamples the pixels rather than
covering them, and the export is flattened, so the original is not recoverable
from the saved file.

**Why does it ask for so few permissions?**
It only needs the tab you clicked on. Anything wider is optional, off by
default, and revocable.

**Do I need an account?**
No. There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to log in to.

**Who makes it?**
PalWorks (https://palworks.ai), which builds and open-sources small,
privacy-respecting browser tools.
